_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and every banned anti-pattern still absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. Schema and rationale: docs/reprint-survival.md. Regen steps: cli-factory/saas-alerts/handfixes/regen.sh (re-applies apply_client_patch.py + apply_doc_patch.py).

handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard compares trustees by SID, resolving SDDL aliases through the OS, so the built-in Administrator (RID 500, rendered as LA) can save and load credentials
handfixes.why: Press 4.30.2+ creds_perms_eval.go compared the SDDL text of the token file's owner and ACE trustees against the process's SID string. The SDDL converter renders the built-in local Administrator (RID 500) as the alias LA, so that account's own ACE never matched: `auth set-token` exited 1 with `token file DACL grants access to a non-owner principal (LA)` and every read refused the file. Reproduced 2026-10-15 on the published fortinet-cli 0.1.0, installed with the README one-liner on a windows-latest runner (whoami S-1-5-21-...-500). The fix resolves each trustee to its SID (fixed aliases from a table, machine-relative ones like LA through ConvertStringSidToSid, kept only when the converter renders that SID back to the same alias) and compares SIDs. The allow-list is unchanged (current user, BUILTIN\Administrators, SYSTEM): an owner or allow-ACE trustee that is any other principal, a broad group, or unresolvable is still refused. A reprint from an unfixed press silently restores the string compare while unit tests stay green on every non-Windows host.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press defect in internal/generator/templates/cliutil_creds_perms_eval.go.tmpl and cliutil_creds_perms_windows.go.tmpl (unfixed on press main as of 4.33.5). Reported upstream: https://github.com/mvanhorn/cli-printing-press/issues/5029

handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard checks the DACL section's framing, so a NULL DACL is refused in the form Windows actually renders it, flags first (D:PAINO_ACCESS_CONTROL), and DACL text that does not frame as flags plus complete six-field ACEs is refused rather than skipped
handfixes.why: Press creds_perms_eval.go refused a NULL DACL only when the DACL section began with NO_ACCESS_CONTROL. SDDL puts DACL flags (P, AI, AR) first, and a real NULL DACL on Windows Server 2025 renders as O:<owner>D:PAINO_ACCESS_CONTROL (measured on a windows-latest runner, 2026-10-15), so the guard found no ACEs to inspect and accepted a world-accessible token file. That was already a hole for every ordinary account; for the built-in Administrator the owner-alias mismatch happened to refuse it, so resolving LA (windows-sddl-alias-sid-compare) without this fix would have widened the hole. The DACL section's framing is now checked: its flags must be drawn from P/AI/AR/NO_ACCESS_CONTROL, an empty DACL followed by a SACL section ends at that section, and the ACE list must be complete, un-nested (...) groups of exactly six fields. Unknown flags, an unclosed or nested group, stray text, or a wrong field count is refused (fail-closed). ACE flags and rights are not validated; they do not change which principal an allow ACE names.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Same press templates as windows-sddl-alias-sid-compare; reported in the same upstream issue: https://github.com/mvanhorn/cli-printing-press/issues/5029

handfixes.summary: Respond API calls mint an accesstoken from the partner api_key (POST /respondApi/api/v1/auth), attach it, re-mint once on rejection, and mask every token in output
handfixes.why: The Respond API (spec 2.0.0) requires an accesstoken header minted from the partner api_key; without it every call answers 400 'Only secure origins are allowed' (live receipt 2026-10-14). Press 4.33.5 has no api-key-to-token exchange auth mode, so client.go is hand-patched to call respond_token.go. A reprint re-emits client.go without the hook and every Respond command (rule-triggers, rules, response-actions, contain) silently fails.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Generator auth mode for an api_key -> access-token exchange scoped to a path prefix (cli-factory/saas-alerts/handfixes/patches/saas-alerts-respond-access-token.json)

handfixes.summary: synced events are keyed by _id, else a customer/product/account-scoped eventId, else a content hash
handfixes.why: Reports eventId is the source product's raw id and collides across customers, products and users; the press id override cannot express a prefer-_id fallback chain, so distinct events overwrote each other at sync and triage/cross-tenant undercounted. A reprint restores the generic id extraction.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Ordered id fallback chains (x-resource-id with alternatives) in the generator

handfixes.summary: events sync maps --since to the documented `start` param; rule-trigger sync follows Respond's [ts, id] array cursor as repeated startAfter keys and treats only a literal pagination.hasNextPage:false as the end
handfixes.why: GET /reports/events filters by `start` (date-time), which the press since-detector misses, so incremental sync re-pulled everything. GET /rule-triggers pages with pagination.cursor = [ts, id] passed back as repeated startAfter keys and a nested pagination.hasNextPage flag; generic sync handles only scalar cursors and top-level has_more names, so it stopped after page 1 or pruned rows on an unproven end.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Since detection for `start` date-time params; array cursors and nested has-more flags in generic sync

handfixes.summary: rule-triggers decide, contain and subscriptions health --reenable only preview without --confirm, and the MCP read-only mode treats them as reads only while --confirm is absent
handfixes.why: These three commands change live Respond triggers, Microsoft 365 accounts (block sign-in, expire sessions, reset password) and webhook subscriptions. The preview default and the mcp:read-only-unless-flags annotation are what keep an agent from acting on a customer tenant by accident; governance.md tiers them as writes on that basis. A reprint that loses either turns a preview into a live write.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Novel commands; re-author with the same --confirm contract on any reprint

handfixes.summary: contain refuses a non-Microsoft 365 account and an email that maps to more than one Microsoft 365 account instead of guessing
handfixes.why: Respond response actions run against application MS only. Acting on the wrong account, or on a Google Workspace user that happens to share an email, would block or reset a real person. contain exits non-zero on any unclear case and asks for --org-id/--account-id.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Novel command; re-author with the same refusal on any reprint

handfixes.summary: the MCP server's --transport http bearer token is read through cliutil.EnvOverride, so an unresolved ${user_config.saas_alerts_mcp_http_token} placeholder refuses to start instead of becoming the secret
handfixes.why: The generated requireHTTPCallerToken read SAAS_ALERTS_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN with os.Getenv. The variable is declared as an optional MCPB user_config value, and a host that skips an optional prompt leaves the literal placeholder text in the environment; that text is public (it is in manifest.json), so anyone could authenticate to an HTTP-mode server started that way. Same fix as bitdefender and sophos-central. TestHTTPTokenPlaceholderRefused fails when the read goes back to os.Getenv (proven 2026-10-20).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: the press main_mcp.go.tmpl should read the HTTP token through cliutil.EnvOverride for every connector.

handfixes.summary: every Webhooks API (/outgoingWebhookApi/) response has its subscription `token` replaced with [withheld] in the client's JSON success path, before print, response cache, sync, tail and MCP
handfixes.why: GET /subscriptions and /subscriptions/disabled return each subscription's token, the string SaaS Alerts attaches to every delivery so the MSP's receiver can authenticate it (webhooks spec 0.9.0, schema Token). Before this fix a sentinel token reached `subscriptions list` output, the MCP saas-alerts_execute result, the HTTP cache files and the local SQLite store (mock receipt 2026-10-20). subscriptions health --reenable sends only enabled plus filter fields, so the blanked value is never written back. Delivery URLs are kept: domain checks need them and SaaS Alerts only delivers to verified domains. TestWebhookTokenNeverLeavesTheClient fails when the hook is removed (proven 2026-10-20).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Generator support for x-secret / writeOnly response fields that are blanked before print, cache and store.

handfixes.summary: an env-sourced SAAS_ALERTS_BASE_URL is marked as an env override in config.Load and configForSave writes the file's own value back, so config.toml never captures the override
handfixes.why: The generated configForSave restored only the env-sourced API key, so `auth set-token` run with SAAS_ALERTS_BASE_URL set wrote that one-run URL into config.toml (reproduced 2026-10-20: base_url = the env value after set-token). After that, unsetting the variable had no effect and every later call sent the saved partner key to the old host. internal/config/env_base_url_test.go fails with the fix removed (proven 2026-10-20). Same generator defect bitdefender and threatdown carry.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Generator defect: configForSave should restore every env-overridden field, not only credentials.

handfixes.summary: --csv, --plain and --quiet output drops terminal control characters (ESC, BEL, C1) from values
handfixes.why: Event fields come from monitored tenants and can be attacker-chosen (a malicious inbox rule or shared file name), and the generated printCSV/printPlain/printQuiet wrote them raw, so a value carrying an OSC 52 or CSI sequence could rewrite the terminal or the clipboard (mock receipt 2026-10-20: ESC and BEL reached --csv and --plain). scrubCell keeps tab/CR/LF for CSV quoting; quiet output uses cliutil.ScrubTerminal. Same fix as bitdefender. TestTabularPrintersScrubTerminal fails with the scrub removed (proven 2026-10-20).

handfixes.summary: stdout and stderr are wrapped in c1EscapeWriter, which rewrites UTF-8 C1 controls (U+0080-U+009F) as \u00XX; isTerminal unwraps it
handfixes.why: encoding/json escapes C0 controls but writes C1 raw, and xterm/VTE act on UTF-8 C1 (CSI, OSC, ST), so a tenant string in --json, --agent or the default pretty-JSON output could drive the terminal. The escape keeps JSON valid and lossless. Ported from bitdefender (adversarial review round 7, 2026-10-19). c1_escape.go is hand-written; root.go wires it in Execute and in the --deliver multiwriter, and helpers.go isTerminal unwraps it so TTY detection is unchanged.
